<sense>

<notes> Kidd. 71
<sup>b</sup> עד אקרא דת' Babylonia extends (for genealogical purposes) as far as Fort (the fortified ford of) T. Meg. 6
<sup>a</sup> אקרא דת' (Ms. F. עקרא דתולבנקי, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 100); Keth. 112
<sup>a</sup> א' דתולבנקי.—Gen. R. s. 16 עד מקום … ואיזו זו תִּרְבַּקְנָה as far (east) as where the Euphrates runs, there is the land of Israel; and what place is this? It is 
<italic>Tirbaḳnah</italic>(?).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00212">
<head-word>תּוֹלָדָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> יָלַד)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>birth, procreation, offspring.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—</italic>
<plural-form>Pl. תּוֹלָדוֹת</plural-form>. Gen. R. s. 12 שלשה דברים הללו … שלש ת' וכ' the following three things form the real creations of the world, and each of them delayed three days, and then produced offspring: the earth &c. Ib. לכל יש ת' … יש להן ת' וכ' all things have origins (mentioned in the Bible), heaven and earth have origins &c. Ib. כל מי שיש לו ת' וכ' whatever has an origin, dies and decays, is created, but does not create, but that which has no origin does not die &c. Num. R. s. 14
<sup>12</sup> בעת שהעמיד ת' during the time of his begetting children. Y. Sot. VIII, 22
<sup>c</sup> bot. שלישי לת' ורביעי וכ' he was the third in the order of birth, and the fourth in the order of accession; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>secondary act, subspecies</italic>, opp. אב or עיקר, v. 
<xref rid="A00014">אָב II</xref>. Y. Sabb. II, 5
<sup>a</sup> bot. שחיטה עיקר וחבורה ת' slaughtering is the primary act (forbidden on the Sabbath), and wounding is the secondary act.</definition>
<notes> B. Kam. 2
<sup>a</sup> הך … קרי לה ת' an act which was essential at the building of the Tabernacle is called 
<italic>ab</italic>, and one which was not essential, is called 
<italic>toladah</italic>; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. as ab. Ib. מדקתני אבות מכלל דאיכא ת'</plural-form> since the Mishnah speaks of main damages, we must conclude that there are also secondary ones; תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶן כיוצא בהן וכ' are their subspecies subject to the same laws or not? Sabb. 2
<sup>b</sup> הכא … תני אבות ותני ת' וכ' here (Sabb. I, 1) where the main subject is the Sabbath, the Mishnah specifies the main act and the secondary acts, &c.; Shebu. 5
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> שבעה … רמה ות' over seven persons no kind of worms had power. Midr. Till. to Ps. XXII, 7 מה הת' הזאת וכ' as the worm has (for its defense) nothing but its mouth, so Israel has nothing but the prayer of his mouth; ib. ed. Bub. מה ת' מעקרת … מעקרין וכ' (not מתעקרת, מתעקרין) as the worm uproots the tree, so Israelites, through their mouth and their prayer, undo evil decrees &c. Midd. II, 5 כל עץ … ת' וכ' wood in which a worm was found was unfit for the altar; a. e.—שני(ה) ת' 
<italic>scarlet-dyed</italic> (
<italic>yarn</italic>). Midr. Till. l. c. משכן של ת' ש' a tabernacle of scarlet yarn. Num. R. s. 4
<sup>13</sup>. Par. III, 10 שְׁנִי ת'; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00224">

<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h. </language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="unknown">תֹּם; תָּמַם)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>simplicity, integrity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pesik. R. s. 21 גלוי … בשבועתם בתוּמֵּיהֶם ושבטו של לוי עומד בתוּמּוֹ (not בתומיא) it is revealed and known before thee that all the tribes shall fail to abide by their oath in rectitude, and that the tribe of Levi shall stand by its rectitude. Midr. Till. to Ps. VII, 9 כתוּמִּי, v. עַקְמוּמִית; a. e.—Esp. הסיח לפי תומו to talk in one’s simplicity, 
<italic>to make a statement in ignorance of its legal bearing</italic>. Yeb. 121
<sup>b</sup> במסיח לפי תומו when the gentile makes an incidental statement (not as formal testimony). B. Kam. 114
<sup>b</sup> תינוק … מסיח לפי תומו ואמר וכ' a child talking in his innocence said, I and my mother were captives &c. Gitt. 28
<sup>b</sup> כל מ' ל' ת' הימוני מהימני ליה whenever a gentile makes an informal statement, we believe him (act on it as evidence); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תּוּמִּים,</plural-form> in connection with אורים, 
<italic>Urim and Tummim</italic> in the high priest’s breastplate (v. אוּר I). Yoma 73
<sup>b</sup> ת' שמשלימין את דבריהן they are named 
<pgbrk id="pg1654" />Tummim, because they complete their words (what they predict comes to pass); Y. ib. VII, end, 44
<sup>c</sup> ת' שהן מתימין וכ', v. תָּמַם. Sot. IX, 12; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>b</sup> ת' הביכורים the addition to the normal quantity of first fruits to be offered. Y. Keth. VI, 30

<sup>a</sup>. Y. Meg. I, 70
<sup>d</sup> bot. אדר הראשון ת' וכ' is the first Adar the addition (the intercalated month), or is it the second Adar?; a. fr.—Esp. 
<italic>the time added to, and given the character of a festive day</italic> (v. Yoma 81
<sup>b</sup> מוסיפין מחול וכ' you must begin the Holy Day some time before its lawful beginning and end some time after its lawful end). Yoma 81
<sup>a</sup> על ת' מלאכה for disregarding the addition by doing a labor which is prohibited on the festive day; על ת' עינוי for disregarding the additional time for fasting (by eating); יהא מוזהר על ת' מלאכה that he be warned concerning the additional time during which he must abstain from labor; a. e.—2) 
<italic>Tosefeth</italic> (
<italic>Tosefta</italic>), a collection of oral laws (Mishnahs) outside of the regular Mishnah. Y. Hor. III, end, 48

<italic>halakhoth</italic>, and ‘glory’, the Tosefeth; Koh. R. to VI, 2 זה בעל תוספתא; Yalk. ib. 972 זה תוספתא. M. Kat. 3
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. תּוֹסָפוֹת</plural-form>. Cant. R. to VI, 9 ועלמות … אין קץ לת' ‘and handmaids without number (ib. 8)’, there is no end of Tosafoth. Y. Peah. II, 17

<head-word>תְּיַיטְרוֹן</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (variously perverted) (θέατρον) 
<italic>theater, show, spectacle</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 87 יום ת' היה וכ' (not תיאטי') it was spectacle day, and all went to see (the show), but he (Joseph) did not go; Cant. R. to I, 1, beg. טיאטרון; Pesik. R. s. 6 יום ת' וקורקסין (not וקורקסיו) a day of theatre and circus performances. Cant. R. l. c. יום ט' של נילוס the show day for the Nile festival, v. זִיבּוּל. Y. Ab. Zar. I, 40
<sup>a</sup> העולה לת' אסור וכ' to go to theatre is forbidden on account of idolatry (which is practiced in it); Tosef. ib. II, 5 לתרטיאות של גוים ed. Zuck. (Var. לתרטאיות, לסרטאיות, read: לתִיאַטְרָאוֹת 
<plural-form>pl.). Y. ib. l. c. העולה לת' וצווח וכ'</plural-form> to go to a theatre and cry out (to vote for a broken down gladiator &c.), if it is for the public benefit, is permitted. Ex. R. s. 51, end ראה אותם גובין לתְיַטְרוֹן he saw that they were collecting for the erection of a theatre. Y. Taan. II, 64
<sup>a</sup> bot. תייט', v. שְׁפַר; a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. תִּיאַטְרָאוֹת, תִּיאַטְרָיוֹת</plural-form>. Meg. 6
<sup>a</sup> ת' וקרקסיות Ar. (ed. תראטדיות, תרטר'; Ms. M. טרטסיאות) theatres and circuses. Tanḥ. ed. Bub., Sh’moth 6 (ref. to Ex. I, 7) שנתמלאו בתי טרטיאות וכ' the theatres and circuses were full of them; Yalk. Ex. 162. Ab. Zar. 18
<sup>b</sup> אין הולכין לטרטיאות וכ' (Ms. M. טרטסיאות) you must not go to the gentile theatres and circuses, because &c., v. זָבַל. Y. Ber. IV, 7
<sup>d</sup> מודה … ולא נתת חלקי בבתי תְרַטְיוֹת וכ' I thank thee … that thou hast given me my share with those sitting in the schools and synagogues, and hast not given me my share in the theatres and circuses; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
